label: Outlook 2016-2021 and Microsoft 365 desktop (Windows)
proves: Layout survives an engine with no media-query support, no CSS float or positioning, default table chrome, and its own DPI scaling: every layout table resets its chrome, widths are HTML attributes, and every call to action carries a VML fallback.

expectations.because: Word applies default cell padding, which opens unintended gaps in every nested layout table.
Word applies default cell spacing, which separates adjacent cells that should butt together.
Word draws table borders unless the HTML border attribute is explicitly zero.
Layout tables must not be announced as data tables by the Windows screen readers Outlook integrates with.
Word ignores CSS width and max-width on tables, so the document width has to be an HTML attribute.
Without an explicit PixelsPerInch setting, Word scales pixel dimensions on high-DPI displays and breaks fixed widths.
Word distributes column widths by content unless the table layout is fixed.
Word ignores the CSS width on a cell, so each column has to carry an HTML width attribute to stay side by side.
Word honours the valign attribute but not CSS vertical-align on a table cell.
Word does not render padding or border-radius on an inline-block anchor, so a VML roundrect is the only reliable button shape.
Without w:anchorlock the VML shape is draggable and the whole shape stops acting as one link target.
An unbalanced downlevel-revealed conditional leaks raw comment markup into non-Outlook clients or hides content in Outlook.
Word ignores float, so any layout that depends on it collapses to stacked blocks.
Word ignores position, so positioned content lands in document order instead.
Word supports neither flexbox nor grid; either one degrades to an unstyled block stack.
Word supports neither flexbox nor grid; either one degrades to an unstyled block stack.
Word collapses an empty cell that sizes itself only through CSS height.
The conditional-wrapping check below compares two counts, so the stylesheet must be proven present or both counts could be zero.
Word cannot load a web font and would render an unpredictable substitute; the stylesheet must stay hidden from it.

limitations.detail: Word evaluates no media queries, so the mobile stacking and full-width container rules never apply in desktop Outlook.
limitations.degrades_to: Desktop Outlook always renders the fixed container width and side-by-side columns, which is the intended desktop result.

limitations.detail: Rounded button corners exist only inside the VML fallback; the CSS border-radius on the non-MSO table is ignored by Word.
limitations.degrades_to: Buttons are rounded through VML arcsize rather than CSS.

limitations.detail: Outlook.com webmail and Outlook for Mac use different engines from the Word-based Windows clients and are not represented by this profile.
limitations.degrades_to: Those clients are unproven by this matrix.
